title: Supramolecular-solvent based extraction of hydroxytyrosol from brines of table olives
author: Ballesteros-Gómez, Ana
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Prepare SUPRAS solvent
steps.instruction: Mix 1,2‑hexanediol with water to obtain a solution containing 4.8 % v/v 1,2‑hexanediol; add Na₂SO₄ to a final concentration of 1 M and add sodium citrate (amount as used for induction) to induce formation of the supramolecular solvent (SUPRAS).

substeps.instruction: Measure the required volume of 1,2‑hexanediol to achieve 4.8 % v/v in the final mixture.
Add water to reach the desired total volume.
Dissolve Na₂SO₄ to reach 1 M concentration.
Add sodium citrate (quantity as described in the original method) to promote supramolecular assembly.
Stir until a homogeneous SUPRAS is obtained.

steps.title: Extract hydroxytyrosol from brine
steps.instruction: Combine the prepared SUPRAS with the olive‑processing brine at a volume ratio of 1 : 20 (SUPRAS : brine) and mix thoroughly to allow liquid–liquid extraction of hydroxytyrosol.

substeps.instruction: Add brine sample so that SUPRAS:brine = 1:20 (v/v).
Mix the two phases vigorously (e.g., vortex or shake) for sufficient time to achieve extraction.

steps.title: Separate SUPRAS phase
steps.instruction: Allow the mixture to separate (by standing or centrifugation) and collect the SUPRAS layer, which contains hydroxytyrosol at approximately 0.5–0.9 % w/w.

steps.title: Analyze extracts
steps.instruction: Analyze the collected SUPRAS extract by liquid chromatography and high‑resolution mass spectrometry to identify hydroxytyrosol and other compounds of interest.
